```{r}
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top"), size = 1.5) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE, legend.outside = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: top-am
#| include: false
top_am <- demand %>% left_join(st_drop_geometry(stations), by = "stn_code") %>%
  slice_max(am_tapin, n = 6)
rp_rank <- rank(-demand$am_tapin)[demand$stn_code == "EW14/NS26"]
```

Morning boardings concentrate in the dense HDB towns of the north and west. The six busiest stations are `r str_c(str_to_title(top_am$stn_name), collapse = ", ")`, led by `r str_to_title(top_am$stn_name[1])` with `r fmt(top_am$am_tapin[1])` morning tap-ins in the month. By contrast, Raffles Place, the CBD's busiest *destination*, ranks only `r rp_rank`th of 164 for morning boardings. The same pattern confirms why the model is calibrated on morning tap-ins: the spatial distribution follows where residents live, which is exactly the process the Huff model represents. LRT stations (the small symbols inside Sengkang, Punggol and Bukit Panjang) board noticeably fewer riders than nearby MRT hubs of similar catchment, because many residents bypass the LRT and travel straight to the hub.

```{r}
#| label: fig-desire
#| fig-cap: "Desire lines of the 60 largest station-to-station morning-peak flows (line width proportional to trips)."
#| fig-height: 6.5
top_flows <- am_peak %>%
  count(orig = ORIGIN_PT_CODE, dest = DESTINATION_PT_CODE, wt = TOTAL_TRIPS, name = "trips") %>%
  filter(orig != dest) %>%
  slice_max(trips, n = 60)

flow_sf <- top_flows %>%
  mutate(geometry = st_sfc(map2(orig, dest, \(a, b) st_linestring(rbind(xy_base[a, ], xy_base[b, ]))),
                           crs = 3414)) %>%
  st_as_sf()

tm_shape(subzones) + tm_polygons(fill = "grey97", col = "grey85", lwd = 0.3) +
  tm_shape(net_base_sf) + tm_lines(col = "grey80", lwd = 0.8) +
  tm_shape(flow_sf) +
  tm_lines(lwd = "trips", col = "#176b87", col_alpha = 0.6,
           lwd.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values.scale = 6),
           lwd.legend = tm_legend(title = "AM-peak trips (month)")) +
  tm_title("The 60 heaviest morning flows") +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top"), size = 1.5) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE, legend.outside = TRUE)
```

The heaviest morning flows are not radial commutes into the CBD. They are **short movements into regional centres and employment nodes**:

- Choa Chu Kang, Boon Lay, Yew Tee and Bukit Batok into the Jurong East regional centre;
- Lakeside, Boon Lay and Pioneer into Joo Koon, the gateway to the Jurong and Tuas industrial estates;
- Pasir Ris into Tampines;
- Ang Mo Kio, Toa Payoh and Newton into Novena, Singapore's medical hub.

Rail serves regional-centre trips as much as city-bound ones. It also means that where people *board* is shaped by short-range competition between neighbouring stations, which is the process the Huff model represents.

# Spatial interaction data frames {#sec-sidf}

This section builds the four data frames required by Tasks 1–3. The origin and destination identifiers share column names (`SUBZONE_N`, `stn_code`) across all of them so that they join without renaming.

```{r}
#| label: sidf
origin_df <- origins_pt %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(SUBZONE_N, PLN_AREA_N, REGION_N, market_potential = pop, centroid)

destination_df <- stations_exp %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(stn_code, stn_name, status, n_lines_2030 = n_lines, lrt) %>%
  left_join(station_attr %>% select(stn_code, n_lines, closeness), by = "stn_code") %>%
  left_join(hdb800, by = "stn_code") %>%
  left_join(attractors, by = "stn_code") %>%
  left_join(demand %>% select(stn_code, observed_am_tapin = am_tapin, total_ridership),
            by = "stn_code")

dist_long <- function(o_pt, s_pt) {
  D <- st_distance(o_pt, s_pt) %>% units::drop_units()
  dimnames(D) <- list(o_pt$SUBZONE_N, s_pt$stn_code)
  as_tibble(D, rownames = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
    pivot_longer(-SUBZONE_N, names_to = "stn_code", values_to = "dist_m") %>%
    mutate(dist_km = pmax(dist_m, 100) / 1000)          # 100 m floor avoids d = 0
}

si_existing <- dist_long(origins_pt, stations) %>%
  left_join(origin_df %>% select(SUBZONE_N, market_potential), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  left_join(destination_df %>% select(stn_code, n_lines, lrt, observed_am_tapin), by = "stn_code")

si_expanded <- dist_long(origins_pt, stations_exp) %>%
  left_join(origin_df %>% select(SUBZONE_N, market_potential), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  left_join(destination_df %>% select(stn_code, status, n_lines = n_lines_2030, lrt), by = "stn_code")

tibble(data_frame = c("origin_df", "destination_df", "si_existing", "si_expanded"),
       rows = c(nrow(origin_df), nrow(destination_df), nrow(si_existing), nrow(si_expanded)),
       key_columns = c("SUBZONE_N, market_potential",
                       "stn_code, observed_am_tapin, n_lines (2022), n_lines_2030, lrt, hdb_ha_800m, job/edu/res floor area, bus services, closeness",
                       "SUBZONE_N, stn_code, dist_km, market_potential, n_lines, lrt",
                       "SUBZONE_N, stn_code, dist_km, market_potential, n_lines, lrt, status"))
```

`si_existing` has 286 origins × 164 stations = `r fmt(nrow(si_existing))` rows, and `si_expanded` has 286 × 193 = `r fmt(nrow(si_expanded))` rows. Distances are straight-line distances from population-weighted centroids, with a 100 m floor so that the power function $d^{-\lambda}$ stays finite.

**A fifth data frame: station-to-station flows.** The MCI destination-choice model (@sec-va-mci) and the exploratory flow models (@sec-sim) work with station-to-station morning-peak trips rather than subzone-to-station shares. Following Chapter 16, intra-station pairs (tap-in and tap-out at the same station) are excluded and zero-flow pairs are kept. Both straight-line and **network distance** (the shortest path along the rail graph) are attached.

```{r}
#| label: sim-data
net_dist <- distances(g_base, weights = edges_base$w_km)
euc_dist <- st_distance(stations) %>% units::drop_units() / 1000
dimnames(euc_dist) <- list(stations$stn_code, stations$stn_code)

sim_data <- expand_grid(orig = stations$stn_code, dest = stations$stn_code) %>%
  filter(orig != dest) %>%
  left_join(am_peak %>% count(orig = ORIGIN_PT_CODE, dest = DESTINATION_PT_CODE,
                              wt = TOTAL_TRIPS, name = "trips"), by = c("orig", "dest")) %>%
  mutate(trips = replace_na(trips, 0),
         euc_km = euc_dist[cbind(orig, dest)],
         net_km = net_dist[cbind(orig, dest)]) %>%
  left_join(hdb800 %>% transmute(orig = stn_code, o_hdb = pmax(hdb_ha_800m, 0.99)), by = "orig") %>%
  left_join(station_attr %>% transmute(dest = stn_code, d_lines = n_lines,
                                       d_lrt = as.numeric(lrt)), by = "dest")

tibble(pairs = nrow(sim_data), zero_pairs = pct(mean(sim_data$trips == 0)),
       total_trips = fmt(sum(sim_data$trips)),
       corr_euclid_network = round(cor(sim_data$euc_km, sim_data$net_km), 3))
```

# Huff model of station choice {#sec-huff}

## Model set-up

The Huff model allocates each subzone's residents across the stations they could board at. All 164 stations are in every subzone's choice set, and the distance-decay term pushes the probability of far-away stations towards zero. The system trip rate $k$ is fixed so that predicted boardings sum to observed boardings:

$$k = \frac{\sum_j B_j^{obs}}{\sum_i Pop_i}$$

The trip rate is fixed so that calibration only has to explain the **spatial allocation** of demand. Two distance-decay functions are considered, both supported by `MCI::huff.shares()`:

- the **power** function $f(d)=d^{-\lambda}$ (the Chapter 18 default);
- the **exponential** function $f(d)=e^{-\lambda d}$.

A fast matrix implementation is used inside the optimiser. The final model is re-estimated with `MCI::huff.shares()` and `MCI::shares.total()`, exactly as in Chapter 18, and the two implementations are checked to agree.

```{r}
#| label: huff-setup
dmat <- function(o_pt, s_pt) {
  D <- st_distance(o_pt, s_pt) %>% units::drop_units()
  pmax(D, 100) / 1000
}

D_base <- dmat(origins_pt, stations)
dest_base <- destination_df %>% filter(status == "Existing") %>%
  slice(match(stations$stn_code, stn_code))
y_obs <- dest_base$observed_am_tapin
pop_i <- origins_pt$pop
k_rate <- sum(y_obs) / sum(pop_i)

decay_term <- function(D, decay) if (decay == "exp") D else log(D)

huff_general <- function(par, X, D, pop, decay = "exp", k = k_rate) {
  lambda <- par[length(par)]
  logA <- as.numeric(X %*% par[-length(par)])
  U <- exp(sweep(-lambda * decay_term(D, decay), 2, logA, "+"))
  as.numeric(k * colSums(U / rowSums(U) * pop))
}

# Attraction design matrix of the final specification (Model 4: lines + LRT + HDB within 800 m)
X_attr <- function(n_lines, lrt, hdb_ha) {
  cbind(log(n_lines), as.numeric(lrt), log(pmax(hdb_ha, 0.5) / 10))
}

fit_stats <- function(obs, pred) tibble(
  RMSE = sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2)), MAE = mean(abs(obs - pred)),
  R2 = cor(obs, pred)^2)
# Display helper: monthly errors -> per weekday
per_day_tbl <- function(t) t %>% mutate(across(any_of(c("RMSE", "MAE")), \(x) round(x / weekdays_may22)),
                                     across(any_of("R2"), \(x) round(x, 3)))

c(trip_rate_k = round(k_rate, 3), observed_total = fmt(sum(y_obs)))
```

## Reference (null) models

A calibrated model is only useful if it beats simpler alternatives. Two reference models are evaluated:

- **R0, nearest station (all-or-nothing).** Every resident boards at the nearest station. This is the Thiessen-polygon logic often used for catchments.
- **R1, Chapter 18 default Huff.** Every station is equally attractive ($A_j=1$), with power decay and $\lambda = 2$, estimated with `MCI::huff.shares()`.

```{r}
#| label: huff-reference
nearest <- apply(D_base, 1, which.min)
pred_r0 <- as.numeric(k_rate * tapply(pop_i, factor(nearest, levels = seq_len(ncol(D_base))), sum))
pred_r0[is.na(pred_r0)] <- 0

im_r1 <- si_existing %>% transmute(SUBZONE_N, stn_code, A = 1, dist_km) %>% as.data.frame()
shares_r1 <- huff.shares(im_r1, "SUBZONE_N", "stn_code", "A", "dist_km",
                         gamma = 1, lambda = -2, check_df = FALSE)
total_r1 <- shares_r1 %>%
  left_join(origin_df %>% select(SUBZONE_N, market_potential), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  shares.total("SUBZONE_N", "stn_code", "p_ij", "market_potential", check_df = FALSE)
pred_r1 <- k_rate * total_r1$sum_E_j[match(stations$stn_code, total_r1$suppliers_single)]

bind_rows(fit_stats(y_obs, pred_r0) %>% mutate(model = "R0 nearest station"),
          fit_stats(y_obs, pred_r1) %>% mutate(model = "R1 Huff, A = 1, power λ = 2")) %>%
  relocate(model) %>% per_day_tbl()
```

The nearest-station rule explains under half of the variation. It gives every resident to one station and ignores that people regularly walk or take a feeder bus past a closer station to reach a better-served one. The default Huff model does only slightly better because it still treats an LRT halt and a three-line interchange as equally attractive.

## Calibration and model selection

Parameters are calibrated by minimising RMSE with `optim()` (Nelder–Mead, restarted from the previous optimum to confirm convergence). Model selection proceeds in two steps.

**Step 1: the distance-decay function.** With a common attraction specification (lines + LRT), the power and exponential functions are compared.

```{r}
#| label: huff-decay
X_specs <- list(
  "1 Lines"                   = cbind(log(dest_base$n_lines)),
  "2 Lines + LRT"             = cbind(log(dest_base$n_lines), dest_base$lrt),
  "3 Lines + LRT + closeness" = cbind(log(dest_base$n_lines), dest_base$lrt,
                                      log(dest_base$closeness / median(dest_base$closeness))),
  "4 Lines + LRT + HDB 800m"  = cbind(log(dest_base$n_lines), dest_base$lrt,
                                      log(pmax(dest_base$hdb_ha_800m, 0.5) / 10)),
  "5 Lines + LRT + bus stops 400m" = cbind(log(dest_base$n_lines), dest_base$lrt,
                                      log(dest_base$bus_stops_400m + 1)),
  "6 Lines + LRT + HDB 800m + bus stops 400m" = cbind(log(dest_base$n_lines), dest_base$lrt,
                                      log(pmax(dest_base$hdb_ha_800m, 0.5) / 10),
                                      log(dest_base$bus_stops_400m + 1)))

calibrate <- function(X, decay = "exp", D = D_base, pop = pop_i, y = y_obs, idx = seq_along(y)) {
  loss <- function(p) sqrt(mean((y[idx] - huff_general(p, X, D, pop, decay)[idx])^2))
  o <- optim(c(rep(0.5, ncol(X)), 2), loss, control = list(maxit = 4000))
  optim(o$par, loss, control = list(maxit = 4000))
}

decay_fits <- map(c(power = "pow", exponential = "exp"), \(dc) calibrate(X_specs[[2]], dc))

decay_table <- imap_dfr(decay_fits, \(o, nm)
  fit_stats(y_obs, huff_general(o$par, X_specs[[2]], D_base, pop_i,
                                if (nm == "power") "pow" else "exp")) %>%
    mutate(decay = nm, gamma = o$par[1], delta = o$par[2], lambda = o$par[3])) %>%
  relocate(decay)
decay_table %>% per_day_tbl() %>% mutate(across(c(gamma, delta, lambda), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-decay
#| fig-cap: "Calibrated distance-decay curves. Both are scaled to 1 at 100 m; the exponential curve drops faster beyond walking range and has a much thinner long tail."
#| fig-height: 3.8
tibble(d = seq(0.1, 6, 0.02)) %>%
  mutate(power = (d / 0.1)^(-decay_table$lambda[1]),
         exponential = exp(-decay_table$lambda[2] * (d - 0.1))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-d, names_to = "decay", values_to = "weight") %>%
  ggplot(aes(d, weight, colour = decay)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.0001)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(power = "grey50", exponential = "#176b87")) +
  labs(x = "Distance from subzone to station (km)", y = "Relative attractiveness (log)",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The exponential function fits clearly better, with R² `r round(decay_table$R2[2], 3)` against `r round(decay_table$R2[1], 3)` and an RMSE lower by about `r fmt((decay_table$RMSE[1] - decay_table$RMSE[2]) / weekdays_may22)` boardings per weekday. @fig-decay shows why. The power function keeps a long tail, so a station 5 km away still receives a small but non-trivial share of every subzone's residents. That is unrealistic for station *access*, which is made on foot or by short feeder bus. The exponential function drops off quickly beyond walking range. This choice also matters for the scenario: with a long-tailed power function, every new station would draw small amounts of demand from stations across the island, and impacts would be spread unrealistically thin.

**Step 2: the attraction specification**, under exponential decay. Five candidates add one driver of station attractiveness at a time: lines served, the LRT-only penalty, network closeness centrality, residential intensity (HDB footprint within 800 m), and feeder-bus access (bus stops within 400 m). A sixth combines residential intensity and feeder-bus access.

In multiplicative form, the attractiveness of station *j* in the richest specification is

$$A_j = n_j^{\gamma} \, e^{\delta \, LRT_j} \, \left(\frac{HDB_j}{10}\right)^{\theta} \, (Bus_j + 1)^{\beta}$$

where $n_j$ is the number of lines served, $LRT_j$ flags LRT-only stations, $HDB_j$ is the HDB footprint (ha) within 800 m and $Bus_j$ is the number of bus stops within 400 m.

```{r}
#| label: huff-calibration
calib <- map(X_specs, calibrate)

spec_table <- imap_dfr(calib, \(o, nm) {
  pred <- huff_general(o$par, X_specs[[nm]], D_base, pop_i)
  fit_stats(y_obs, pred) %>%
    mutate(spec = nm, parameters = length(o$par),
           estimates = str_c(round(o$par, 2), collapse = " / "))
}) %>% relocate(spec, parameters, estimates)
spec_table %>% per_day_tbl() %>% rename(`RMSE (per weekday)` = RMSE, `MAE (per weekday)` = MAE)
```

```{r}
#| label: huff-choose
#| include: false
final_spec <- "4 Lines + LRT + HDB 800m"
par_final <- calib[[final_spec]]$par
gamma_hat <- par_final[1]; delta_hat <- par_final[2]; theta_hat <- par_final[3]; lambda_hat <- par_final[4]
r2_of <- function(i) spec_table$R2[i]
r2_final <- r2_of(4); r2_r0 <- fit_stats(y_obs, pred_r0)$R2; r2_r1 <- fit_stats(y_obs, pred_r1)$R2
r2_gain_clo <- r2_of(3) - r2_of(2)
r2_gain_hdb <- r2_of(4) - r2_of(2)
r2_gain_bus <- r2_of(5) - r2_of(2)
r2_gain_m6  <- r2_of(6) - r2_of(4)
beta_bus_m6 <- calib[[6]]$par[4]
```

Specification 4 (**Lines + LRT + HDB within 800 m, exponential decay**) is selected as the final model.

**Why residential intensity belongs in the model.** Its gain in R² over specification 2 is modest (`r sprintf("%+.3f", r2_gain_hdb)`), but it captures the mechanism this study is about. Singapore's earlier MRT lines were threaded through HDB towns and estates that already existed, so their stations opened into large ready-made populations within walking distance. Many recent stations have been placed in new HDB towns and estates whose homes are still being built and occupied; their surroundings hold little housing, and their ridership is low. The HDB-footprint term makes a station's attractiveness depend on how much housing lies within a 10-minute walk, so the model reproduces this contrast instead of treating a station in an empty new town like one in a mature estate.

The residents counted by the HDB term are also part of the subzone populations, so the two terms overlap. They play different roles, however. The origin population says *how many* residents a subzone has; the HDB term says whether a *station* sits in the middle of housing or at its edge, which a single point per subzone cannot resolve. A station surrounded by blocks collects walk-in riders that a model using subzone points alone would share out with its neighbours.

The other candidates add little:

- **Closeness centrality** adds `r sprintf("%+.3f", r2_gain_clo)` to R² over specification 2, so a station's position in the network graph does not draw residents once lines served are known.
- **Bus stops within 400 m** add only `r sprintf("%+.3f", r2_gain_bus)` on their own, and specification 6 (HDB plus bus stops) adds `r sprintf("%+.3f", r2_gain_m6)` over specification 4, with a bus-stop coefficient of `r round(beta_bus_m6, 2)`. Almost every station in Singapore is surrounded by bus stops, so the *number* of nearby stops does not separate stations whose feeder services pull residents from far away (Woodlands, Boon Lay) from the rest. What matters is *where* those buses come from, which a stop count cannot capture.

All four parameters of the final model are plausible:

- $\hat\gamma =$ `r round(gamma_hat, 2)`: a two-line interchange is about $2^{\hat\gamma} \approx$ `r round(2^gamma_hat, 1)` times as attractive as a single-line station.
- $\hat\delta =$ `r round(delta_hat, 2)`: an LRT-only station is about $e^{\hat\delta} \approx$ `r round(exp(delta_hat), 2)` times as attractive as an MRT station, so most LRT-area residents are drawn to the town's MRT hub.
- $\hat\theta =$ `r round(theta_hat, 2)`: doubling the HDB footprint within 800 m raises a station's attractiveness by about `r pct(2^theta_hat - 1, 0)`.
- $\hat\lambda =$ `r round(lambda_hat, 2)` per km: every additional 500 m to a station cuts its attractiveness by about `r pct(1 - exp(-lambda_hat / 2), 0)`, a steep access decay consistent with walking and short feeder trips.

```{r}
#| label: fig-surface
#| fig-cap: "Calibration surface of the final model: RMSE over the attraction exponent γ and the exponential distance-decay rate λ, holding the LRT penalty δ and the HDB elasticity θ at their optima. The cross marks the calibrated solution."
#| fig-height: 5
X_final_base <- X_attr(dest_base$n_lines, dest_base$lrt, dest_base$hdb_ha_800m)
surface <- expand_grid(gamma = seq(0, 2.5, 0.1), lambda = seq(0.5, 4, 0.1)) %>%
  mutate(rmse = map2_dbl(gamma, lambda, \(g, l)
    sqrt(mean((y_obs - huff_general(c(g, delta_hat, theta_hat, l), X_final_base, D_base, pop_i))^2))))

ggplot(surface, aes(gamma, lambda, fill = rmse / 1000)) +
  geom_raster() +
  geom_contour(aes(z = rmse / 1000), colour = "white", alpha = 0.5, bins = 12) +
  annotate("point", x = gamma_hat, y = lambda_hat, shape = 4, size = 4, stroke = 1.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "RMSE ('000)") +
  labs(x = "Attraction exponent γ (lines)", y = "Distance-decay rate λ (per km)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The surface has a single, well-defined minimum, so the optimiser has found the global solution and not a local one. The diagonal valley shows a trade-off between the two parameters: steeper distance decay can be partly offset by stronger attraction. This is why the cross-validation below checks that the parameters are stable.

## Final model with the MCI package

```{r}
#| label: huff-final
attraction <- function(n_lines, lrt, hdb_ha) exp(as.numeric(X_attr(n_lines, lrt, hdb_ha) %*% par_final[1:3]))

im_existing <- si_existing %>%
  left_join(destination_df %>% select(stn_code, hdb_ha_800m), by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(A = attraction(n_lines, lrt, hdb_ha_800m)) %>%
  select(SUBZONE_N, stn_code, A, dist_km) %>% as.data.frame()

shares_base <- huff.shares(im_existing, "SUBZONE_N", "stn_code", "A", "dist_km",
                           gamma = 1, lambda = -lambda_hat, dtype = "exp", check_df = FALSE)

total_base <- shares_base %>%
  left_join(origin_df %>% select(SUBZONE_N, market_potential), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  shares.total("SUBZONE_N", "stn_code", "p_ij", "market_potential", check_df = FALSE)

pred_base <- tibble(stn_code = total_base$suppliers_single,
                    pred_base = k_rate * total_base$sum_E_j)

calibrated <- dest_base %>%
  left_join(pred_base, by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(residual = observed_am_tapin - pred_base,
         pct_error = residual / observed_am_tapin)

c(max_abs_diff_vs_matrix = max(abs(calibrated$pred_base -
    huff_general(par_final, X_final_base, D_base, pop_i)[match(calibrated$stn_code, stations$stn_code)])))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-obs-pred
#| fig-cap: "Observed versus calibrated morning-peak tap-ins for the 164 existing stations."
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggscatterstats(calibrated %>% mutate(pred_day = pred_base / weekdays_may22,
                                    obs_day = observed_am_tapin / weekdays_may22),
               x = pred_day, y = obs_day,
               xlab = "Predicted AM-peak tap-ins per weekday",
               ylab = "Observed AM-peak tap-ins per weekday",
               marginal = FALSE, bf.message = FALSE,
               point.args = list(alpha = 0.6, colour = "#176b87", size = 2)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey40")
```

The calibrated model tracks observed boardings across the full range: the points lie along the 1:1 line from small LRT halts to the busiest suburban hubs, with a correlation of about `r round(sqrt(r2_final), 2)`. The largest misses are systematic, not random. They are discussed with the residual map in @fig-residual-map, and their spatial clustering is tested formally in @sec-va-moran.

## Out-of-sample validation and parameter stability

Calibrating and judging fit on the same 164 stations flatters any model. Five-fold cross-validation is used instead: stations are randomly split into five groups, parameters are re-estimated on four groups, and boardings are predicted for the held-out group.

```{r}
#| label: huff-cv
folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = length(y_obs)))
X4 <- X_specs[[final_spec]]   # exponential decay (default)

cv <- map_dfr(1:5, \(f) {
  o <- calibrate(X4, idx = which(folds != f))
  pred <- huff_general(o$par, X4, D_base, pop_i)
  tibble(fold = f, gamma = o$par[1], delta = o$par[2], theta = o$par[3], lambda = o$par[4],
         test_R2 = cor(y_obs[folds == f], pred[folds == f])^2,
         test_RMSE_per_weekday = sqrt(mean((y_obs[folds == f] - pred[folds == f])^2)) / weekdays_may22)
})

cv %>% mutate(across(-fold, \(x) round(x, 3)))
cv %>% summarise(across(c(gamma, delta, theta, lambda, test_R2), list(mean = mean, sd = sd))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Out-of-sample R² averages `r round(mean(cv$test_R2), 2)`, close to the in-sample `r round(r2_final, 2)`, so the model is not over-fitted. The parameter estimates barely move between folds ($\lambda$ ranges from `r round(min(cv$lambda), 2)` to `r round(max(cv$lambda), 2)`). The fold-to-fold range of $\lambda$ is later used as an uncertainty band for the new-station predictions.

## Model 4 or Model 6? Out-of-sample comparison and new-station sensitivity {#sec-m4-m6}

Specification 6 adds bus stops within 400 m to the final model. Its in-sample gain is tiny (@sec-huff), but in-sample fit always rises when a parameter is added. Two further tests decide between the models: how well each predicts stations it has not seen, and whether the choice changes the forecasts for the 29 new stations.

```{r}
#| label: m4-m6-cv
X6 <- X_specs[["6 Lines + LRT + HDB 800m + bus stops 400m"]]
cv_pred <- function(X) {
  pred <- numeric(length(y_obs))
  for (f in 1:5) {
    o <- calibrate(X, idx = which(folds != f))
    pred[folds == f] <- huff_general(o$par, X, D_base, pop_i)[folds == f]
  }
  pred
}
cv4 <- cv_pred(X4); cv6 <- cv_pred(X6)

tibble(model = c("Model 4: Lines + LRT + HDB 800m", "Model 6: + bus stops 400m"),
       parameters = c(ncol(X4), ncol(X6)) + 1) %>%
  bind_cols(bind_rows(fit_stats(y_obs, cv4), fit_stats(y_obs, cv6))) %>%
  mutate(RMSE = fmt(RMSE / weekdays_may22), MAE = fmt(MAE / weekdays_may22), R2 = round(R2, 3)) %>%
  rename(`CV RMSE (per weekday)` = RMSE, `CV MAE (per weekday)` = MAE, `CV R²` = R2)
```

```{r}
#| label: m4-m6-new
par6 <- calib[[6]]$par
D_exp_m <- dmat(origins_pt, stations_exp)
attr_exp <- destination_df[match(stations_exp$stn_code, destination_df$stn_code), ]
X4_exp <- X_attr(stations_exp$n_lines, stations_exp$lrt, attr_exp$hdb_ha_800m)
X6_exp <- cbind(X4_exp, log(attr_exp$bus_stops_400m + 1))

m46 <- tibble(stn_code = stations_exp$stn_code, status = stations_exp$status,
              m4 = huff_general(par_final, X4_exp, D_exp_m, pop_i) / weekdays_may22,
              m6 = huff_general(par6, X6_exp, D_exp_m, pop_i) / weekdays_may22) %>%
  filter(status != "Existing") %>%
  left_join(destination_df %>% select(stn_code, stn_name, bus_stops_400m), by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(diff = m6 - m4, diff_pct = diff / m4)

rho_46 <- cor(m46$m4, m46$m6, method = "spearman")
p25_day <- quantile(y_obs, 0.25) / weekdays_may22
flip <- m46 %>% filter((m4 < p25_day) != (m6 < p25_day))

m46 %>% slice_max(abs(diff_pct), n = 6) %>%
  transmute(station = str_to_title(stn_name), bus_stops_400m,
            `Model 4` = fmt(m4), `Model 6` = fmt(m6), difference = pct(diff_pct, 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: m4-m6-numbers
#| include: false
cv_r2_4 <- fit_stats(y_obs, cv4)$R2; cv_r2_6 <- fit_stats(y_obs, cv6)$R2
cv_rmse_4 <- fit_stats(y_obs, cv4)$RMSE; cv_rmse_6 <- fit_stats(y_obs, cv6)$RMSE
```

**Result.** Out of sample, Model 6 is `r if (cv_rmse_6 < cv_rmse_4) "marginally better" else "no better"` than Model 4 (cross-validated R² `r round(cv_r2_6, 3)` against `r round(cv_r2_4, 3)`; RMSE `r fmt(cv_rmse_6 / weekdays_may22)` against `r fmt(cv_rmse_4 / weekdays_may22)` boardings per weekday). The two models rank the 29 new stations almost identically (Spearman ρ = `r round(rho_46, 3)`). The largest differences, shown above, are at stations with unusually many or few bus stops nearby, and `r if (nrow(flip) == 0) "no new station" else str_c(nrow(flip), " station(s)")` crosses the lower-quartile line when Model 6 replaces Model 4.

**Decision.** Model 4 is kept. The bus-stop term does not improve out-of-sample accuracy in any meaningful way, its coefficient has an implausible negative sign (more bus stops, less attraction), and it leaves the conclusions about the new stations unchanged. Model 6 is reported as a robustness check: the findings below hold under either model.

## Where the model errs

```{r}
#| label: fig-residual-map
#| fig-cap: "Residuals of the calibrated Huff model (observed minus predicted AM-peak tap-ins per weekday). Bubble size is the size of the error; blue = model under-predicts, red = over-predicts."
#| fig-height: 6.5
res_map <- stations %>% left_join(calibrated %>% select(stn_code, residual), by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(res_day = residual / weekdays_may22, abs_res = abs(res_day))

tm_shape(subzones) + tm_polygons(fill = "grey97", col = "grey85", lwd = 0.3) +
  tm_shape(res_map) +
  tm_symbols(size = "abs_res", fill = "res_day",
             fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "fixed",
                                             breaks = c(-12000, -2500, -1000, 1000, 2500, 12000),
                                             values = "brewer.rd_bu",
                                             labels = c("< -2,500", "-2,500 to -1,000", "-1,000 to 1,000",
                                                        "1,000 to 2,500", "> 2,500")),
             fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Residual per weekday"),
             size.legend = tm_legend(title = "|Residual| per weekday"), col = "grey30", lwd = 0.4) +
  tm_shape(res_map %>% slice_max(abs_res, n = 8)) +
  tm_text("stn_code", size = 0.55, ymod = 0.8) +
  tm_title("Huff model residuals by station") +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top"), size = 1.5) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE, legend.outside = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: residual-table
calibrated %>%
  slice_max(abs(residual), n = 10) %>%
  transmute(stn_code, stn_name, observed_per_weekday = fmt(observed_am_tapin / weekdays_may22),
            predicted_per_weekday = fmt(pred_base / weekdays_may22),
            residual_per_weekday = fmt(residual / weekdays_may22))
```

The largest residuals form three geographically coherent groups.

1. **Under-prediction along the northern North-South Line**: Admiralty, Sembawang, Yew Tee, Woodlands, Kranji and Marsiling. These towns sit at the end of a long radial line with no alternative, and the stations nearest the Causeway also serve cross-border commuters arriving from Johor by bus. Those commuters are not Singapore residents, so the Census-driven model cannot see them.
2. **Under-prediction at city-fringe nodes** such as Newton, and at big bus-interchange hubs such as Ang Mo Kio and Boon Lay. Morning tap-ins here include non-residential trips (schools, hotels, bus-to-rail transfers from far beyond walking range) that a resident-population model cannot see.
3. **Over-prediction in the east**: Tampines East, Tampines West, Bedok Reservoir and Pasir Ris. Downtown Line stage 3 stations duplicate the East-West Line inside the same towns, and the east is well served by direct buses to the Tampines regional centre and the Changi employment areas, so a smaller share of residents boards rail than the model expects.

None of these is a failure of the Huff logic itself. They point to demand sources (cross-border commuters, feeder buses, competing bus services) that are not in the model. Because the groups are *regional*, their spatial clustering is tested formally in @sec-va-moran: a regional bias would carry straight into the forecasts for new stations in the same areas.

# Predicting ridership at the JRL and CRL1 stations {#sec-scenario}

## Expanded-network prediction

The calibrated parameters are applied to the expanded network. New stations are single-line MRT stations ($n_j = 1$, not LRT); the seven interchange stations gain one line. Residential population is held at Census 2020 levels and the trip rate $k$ is unchanged. The scenario therefore answers: *if today's residents faced the 2030 network, where would they board?*

```{r}
#| label: scenario-expanded
im_expanded <- si_expanded %>%
  left_join(destination_df %>% select(stn_code, hdb_ha_800m), by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(A = attraction(n_lines, lrt, hdb_ha_800m)) %>%
  select(SUBZONE_N, stn_code, A, dist_km) %>% as.data.frame()

shares_exp <- huff.shares(im_expanded, "SUBZONE_N", "stn_code", "A", "dist_km",
                          gamma = 1, lambda = -lambda_hat, dtype = "exp", check_df = FALSE)

total_exp <- shares_exp %>%
  left_join(origin_df %>% select(SUBZONE_N, market_potential), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  shares.total("SUBZONE_N", "stn_code", "p_ij", "market_potential", check_df = FALSE)

D_exp <- dmat(origins_pt, stations_exp)
lambda_band <- range(cv$lambda)
hdb_exp <- destination_df$hdb_ha_800m[match(stations_exp$stn_code, destination_df$stn_code)]
X_final_exp <- X_attr(stations_exp$n_lines, stations_exp$lrt, hdb_exp)
band <- map(lambda_band, \(l) huff_general(c(par_final[1:3], l), X_final_exp, D_exp, pop_i))

scenario <- stations_exp %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(stn_code, stn_name, status, n_lines) %>%
  left_join(tibble(stn_code = total_exp$suppliers_single, pred_exp = k_rate * total_exp$sum_E_j),
            by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(low = pmin(band[[1]], band[[2]]), high = pmax(band[[1]], band[[2]])) %>%
  left_join(pred_base, by = "stn_code") %>%
  left_join(planned %>% select(stn_code, line), by = "stn_code")

p25_existing <- quantile(calibrated$observed_am_tapin, 0.25)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-new-stations
#| fig-cap: "Predicted weekday AM-peak tap-ins per day at the 29 new stations (Census 2020 population). Error bars show the range implied by the cross-validated λ; the dashed line marks the lower quartile (25th percentile) of existing stations' observed boardings."
#| fig-height: 7
new_pred <- scenario %>% filter(status != "Existing") %>%
  mutate(per_day = pred_exp / weekdays_may22,
         low_d = low / weekdays_may22, high_d = high / weekdays_may22)

ggplot(new_pred, aes(per_day, fct_reorder(stn_name, per_day), fill = line)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = low_d, xmax = high_d), height = 0.3, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p25_existing / weekdays_may22, linetype = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(JRL = "#0099aa", CRL = "#97c616")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted AM-peak tap-ins per weekday", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: new-station-table
new_pred %>%
  arrange(desc(pred_exp)) %>%
  transmute(stn_code, stn_name, line,
            per_weekday = fmt(per_day), range = str_c(fmt(low_d), "–", fmt(high_d)),
            percentile_vs_existing = pct(ecdf(calibrated$observed_am_tapin)(pred_exp), 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: scenario-numbers
#| include: false
crl_mean <- mean(new_pred$per_day[new_pred$line == "CRL"])
jrl_mean <- mean(new_pred$per_day[new_pred$line == "JRL"])
n_low <- sum(new_pred$pred_exp < p25_existing)
low_names <- new_pred %>% filter(pred_exp < p25_existing) %>% arrange(pred_exp) %>% pull(stn_name)
top3 <- new_pred %>% slice_max(pred_exp, n = 3) %>% pull(stn_name)
```

Two clear messages emerge from @fig-new-stations.

- **Stations inserted into mature HDB estates lead.** `r str_to_title(top3[1])`, `r str_to_title(top3[2])` and `r str_to_title(top3[3])` top the ranking. Each is placed in an established estate that is currently beyond comfortable walking distance of an MRT line, and each would rank in the upper quarter of today's stations from day one. On average a CRL1 station attracts about `r fmt(crl_mean)` morning tap-ins per weekday, almost twice the JRL average of `r fmt(jrl_mean)`.
- **Several new stations would be "ghost-risk" stations on today's population.** `r n_low` of the 29 new stations fall below the lower quartile of existing stations: `r str_c(str_to_title(low_names), collapse = ", ")`. They are of three kinds:
  - stations in employment areas with few residents, namely the Jurong industrial estate (Tukang, Jurong Hill, Jurong Pier) and the Changi and Loyang employment areas (Aviation Park, Loyang);
  - the NTU campus stations, whose student and staff trips are not home-based morning boardings;
  - Tengah, a new town that had essentially no residents at the 2020 Census.

The cross-validated uncertainty bands are narrow relative to the differences between stations, so the *ranking* of new stations is robust to parameter uncertainty, even though the absolute numbers should be treated as indicative. For the employment and campus stations, a low morning *boarding* forecast does not mean low use: these stations may be busy as morning *destinations*, which this residential model does not measure. @sec-va-mci tests this directly with an MCI destination-choice model. For Tengah, the case rests on future residents, the subject of the next section.

## Why some new stations will be quiet: housing within walking distance {#sec-hdb-reveal}

The final model ties a station's pull to the housing around it. @fig-hdb-reveal shows why this matters for the new lines: it plots morning boardings against the HDB footprint within 800 m for every existing station (observed, May 2022) and every new station (predicted).

```{r}
#| label: fig-hdb-reveal
#| fig-cap: "AM-peak tap-ins per weekday against HDB footprint within 800 m. Grey: existing stations (observed, May 2022). Coloured: new JRL/CRL1 stations (predicted). New stations with fewer than 15 ha of HDB footprint within 800 m are labelled."
#| fig-height: 5.5
hdb_cmp <- bind_rows(
  calibrated %>% transmute(stn_code, stn_name, hdb_ha_800m, per_day = observed_am_tapin / weekdays_may22,
                           group = "Existing (observed)"),
  new_pred %>% left_join(destination_df %>% select(stn_code, hdb_ha_800m), by = "stn_code") %>%
    transmute(stn_code, stn_name, hdb_ha_800m, per_day, group = str_c("New ", line, " (predicted)")))

ggplot(hdb_cmp, aes(hdb_ha_800m + 1, per_day, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(data = filter(hdb_cmp, group == "Existing (observed)"), size = 1.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = filter(hdb_cmp, group != "Existing (observed)"), size = 2.8) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(hdb_cmp, group != "Existing (observed)", hdb_ha_800m < 15),
                           aes(label = str_to_title(stn_name)), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE,
                           seed = 626, max.overlaps = 20) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = p25_existing / weekdays_may22, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Existing (observed)" = "grey60", "New CRL (predicted)" = "#97c616",
                                 "New JRL (predicted)" = "#0099aa")) +
  labs(x = "HDB footprint within 800 m (ha + 1, log)", y = "AM-peak tap-ins per weekday (log)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: hdb-reveal-table
hdb_cmp %>%
  mutate(group = if_else(group == "Existing (observed)", group, "New (predicted)"),
         housing = cut(hdb_ha_800m, c(-Inf, 5, 15, 30, Inf),
                       labels = c("< 5 ha", "5–15 ha", "15–30 ha", "> 30 ha"))) %>%
  group_by(group, housing) %>%
  summarise(stations = n(), median_tapins_per_weekday = fmt(median(per_day)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(stations, median_tapins_per_weekday))
```

```{r}
#| label: hdb-reveal-numbers
#| include: false
hdb_med_exist <- median(hdb_cmp$hdb_ha_800m[hdb_cmp$group == "Existing (observed)"])
hdb_med_new <- median(hdb_cmp$hdb_ha_800m[hdb_cmp$group != "Existing (observed)"])
rho_hdb <- cor(hdb_cmp$hdb_ha_800m[hdb_cmp$group == "Existing (observed)"],
               hdb_cmp$per_day[hdb_cmp$group == "Existing (observed)"], method = "spearman")
low_hdb_new <- hdb_cmp %>% filter(group != "Existing (observed)", hdb_ha_800m < 5)
```

This is the issue that the ghost-station debate is about, and the data reveal it clearly:

- **Among existing stations, housing within walking distance and morning boardings go together** (Spearman ρ = `r round(rho_hdb, 2)`). Existing stations with less than 5 ha of HDB footprint within 800 m board a median of only `r fmt(median(hdb_cmp$per_day[hdb_cmp$group == "Existing (observed)" & hdb_cmp$hdb_ha_800m < 5]))` people per weekday morning, against `r fmt(median(hdb_cmp$per_day[hdb_cmp$group == "Existing (observed)" & hdb_cmp$hdb_ha_800m >= 5]))` for the rest. Most older stations were threaded through HDB towns that already existed, so they opened into ready-made demand.
- **`r nrow(low_hdb_new)` of the 29 new stations have less than 5 ha of HDB footprint within 800 m**: `r str_c(str_to_title(low_hdb_new$stn_name), collapse = ", ")`. They sit in industrial estates, the NTU campus and the airport and Loyang employment areas.
- **These stations are predicted to have extremely low ridership**, at the bottom left of the chart and mostly far below the lower quartile of existing stations. Tengah is the other case: its HDB blocks are being completed and occupied, but at the 2020 Census its subzones had almost no residents (@sec-tengah).

A model without the HDB term (specification 2) would rate an MRT station in an empty district as highly as one in a mature estate at the same distance from residents. It would therefore overstate exactly the stations at risk.

## Sensitivity: Tengah at build-out {#sec-tengah}

A model driven by today's population cannot see tomorrow's residents, which is exactly the trap of the ghost-station debate. Tengah is planned for about **42,000 homes** across five districts. At roughly 3.1 residents per home (close to the Census 2020 average household size), build-out adds about 130,000 residents. These are allocated equally to Tengah's five residential subzones (Plantation, Park, Garden, Brickland and Forest Hill), and the expanded-network model is re-run.

```{r}
#| label: scenario-tengah
tengah_res <- c("PLANTATION", "PARK", "GARDEN", "BRICKLAND", "FOREST HILL")
tengah_add <- 42000 * 3.1 / length(tengah_res)

origins_tengah <- subzones %>%
  left_join(pop, by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  mutate(pop = replace_na(pop, 0) + if_else(SUBZONE_N %in% tengah_res & PLN_AREA_N == "TENGAH",
                                            tengah_add, 0)) %>%
  filter(pop > 0) %>%
  make_origins() %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("ox", "oy"), crs = 3414)

D_tengah <- dmat(origins_tengah, stations_exp)
pred_tengah <- huff_general(par_final, X_final_exp, D_tengah, origins_tengah$pop)

tengah_cmp <- scenario %>%
  mutate(pred_tengah = pred_tengah) %>%
  filter(stn_code %in% c("JS2", "JS3", "JS4", "JE1", "JE2", "JE3", "JS5", "NS4/BP1")) %>%
  transmute(stn_code, stn_name,
            census_2020 = pred_exp / weekdays_may22,
            tengah_buildout = pred_tengah / weekdays_may22)
tengah_cmp %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), fmt))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tengah
#| fig-cap: "Predicted AM-peak tap-ins per weekday at stations around Tengah under Census 2020 population and at Tengah's planned build-out."
#| fig-height: 4.5
tengah_cmp %>%
  pivot_longer(c(census_2020, tengah_buildout), names_to = "scenario", values_to = "per_day") %>%
  mutate(scenario = recode(scenario, census_2020 = "Census 2020 population",
                           tengah_buildout = "Tengah build-out (~130k residents)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(per_day, fct_reorder(stn_name, per_day), fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p25_existing / weekdays_may22, linetype = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "#0099aa")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted AM-peak tap-ins per weekday", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: tengah-numbers
#| include: false
tg <- tengah_cmp %>% filter(stn_code == "JS3")
tg1 <- tengah_cmp %>% filter(stn_code == "JE1")
```

At build-out, Tengah station (JS3) rises from about `r fmt(tg$census_2020)` to about `r fmt(tg$tengah_buildout)` morning tap-ins per weekday, and Tengah Plantation (JE1) from about `r fmt(tg1$census_2020)` to `r fmt(tg1$tengah_buildout)`. Tengah station thus moves from the ghost-risk zone to well above the existing-station median of `r fmt(median(calibrated$observed_am_tapin) / weekdays_may22)`, and Tengah Plantation becomes one of the busiest stations on the JRL. This is the Hume and Buangkok story in numbers: whether a JRL station is a white elephant depends almost entirely on the **timing of housing completions relative to the line's opening**. Because the model is quick to re-run, it can be used to set a completion threshold, the number of occupied homes at which opening a station becomes justified.

# Impact on existing stations {#sec-impact}

Because the trip rate is fixed, every boarding at a new station is a boarding *diverted* from an existing station. The change at each existing station measures its exposure to the new lines.

```{r}
#| label: impact
impact <- scenario %>%
  filter(status == "Existing") %>%
  mutate(change = pred_exp - pred_base, change_pct = change / pred_base,
         upgraded = stn_code %in% interchange_upgrades$interchange_with)

impact_sf <- stations %>% left_join(impact %>% select(stn_code, change, change_pct, upgraded),
                                    by = "stn_code")

bind_rows(impact %>% slice_min(change, n = 8), impact %>% slice_max(change, n = 7)) %>%
  transmute(stn_code, stn_name, upgraded,
            before = fmt(pred_base / weekdays_may22), after = fmt(pred_exp / weekdays_may22),
            change_per_day = fmt(change / weekdays_may22), change_pct = pct(change_pct))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-impact
#| fig-cap: "Interactive map: predicted change in AM-peak tap-ins at existing stations after JRL and CRL1 open. Bubble size is the absolute change per weekday; colour is the percentage change (red = losing riders, blue = gaining, grey = under 1%). Orange lines and white dots are the new JRL/CRL1 links and stations. Click a station for its figures."
impact_view <- impact_sf %>%
  mutate(day_change = change / weekdays_may22,
         cls = cut(change_pct, c(-Inf, -0.3, -0.15, -0.05, -0.01, 0.01, 0.05, 0.3, Inf),
                   labels = c("< -30%", "-30 to -15%", "-15 to -5%", "-5 to -1%", "-1 to 1%",
                              "1 to 5%", "5 to 30%", "> 30%"))) %>%
  st_transform(4326)
pal_imp <- colorFactor(c("#b2182b", "#d6604d", "#f4a582", "#fddbc7", "#d9d9d9",
                         "#d1e5f0", "#92c5de", "#2166ac"), levels = levels(impact_view$cls))
max_ch <- max(abs(impact_view$day_change))

base_leaflet() %>%
  add_network(new_links = TRUE) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = impact_view, group = "Existing stations",
                   radius = ~radius_of(abs(day_change), max_ch), color = "#555", weight = 0.6,
                   fillColor = ~pal_imp(cls), fillOpacity = 0.85,
                   label = ~str_to_title(stn_name),
                   popup = ~sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>Change: %s tap-ins / weekday (%s)%s",
                                    str_to_title(stn_name), comma(round(day_change)),
                                    pct(change_pct), if_else(upgraded, "<br>Upgraded interchange", ""))) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = st_transform(new_stations, 4326), group = "New stations",
                   radius = 3, color = "#d95f02", weight = 1, fillColor = "white", fillOpacity = 1,
                   label = ~str_to_title(stn_name)) %>%
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal_imp, values = impact_view$cls, opacity = 0.9,
            title = "Change in AM tap-ins") %>%
  add_size_legend(c(500, 2000, 8000), max_ch, "Change per weekday (±)") %>%
  layer_control(c("Existing stations", "New stations", "Rail network"))
```

```{r}
#| label: impact-numbers
#| include: false
diverted <- sum(new_pred$pred_exp)
share_div <- diverted / sum(y_obs)
n_affected <- sum(abs(impact$change_pct) >= 0.05)
n_loss15 <- sum(impact$change_pct <= -0.15)
med_abs <- median(abs(impact$change_pct))
upg <- impact %>% filter(upgraded) %>% arrange(desc(change_pct))
west_loss <- impact %>% filter(stn_code %in% c("EW28", "EW26", "EW25", "EW29")) %>% arrange(change_pct)
```

The new stations capture about `r pct(share_div)` of all morning boardings. Under the fixed-population assumption this is diverted demand, not new demand. The impact is **local**: the median existing station changes by only `r pct(med_abs)`, `r n_affected` of 164 stations change by 5% or more, and `r n_loss15` lose 15% or more. These losses form three clusters, each next to a new line.

- **West (JRL).** The EWL stations between Jurong East and Joo Koon lose most heavily: `r str_c(str_to_title(west_loss$stn_name), " (", pct(west_loss$change_pct, 0), ")", collapse = ", ")`. Their catchments in Jurong West and Boon Lay are taken by Gek Poh, Jurong West, Bahar Junction and Tawas. The Bukit Panjang LRT and Bukit Batok stations lose residents to Choa Chu Kang West, Tengah and Bukit Batok West.
- **North-east (CRL1).** Kovan, Buangkok, Serangoon, Lorong Chuan, Bishan, Yio Chu Kang and the TEL stations at Mayflower, Upper Thomson and Lentor lose residents to Serangoon North, Tavistock and Teck Ghee.
- **East (CRL1).** Tampines, Tampines East and Upper Changi lose residents to Tampines North and Pasir Ris East.

**Interchange upgrades do not guarantee growth.** Of the seven upgraded stations, `r str_c(str_to_title(upg$stn_name[upg$change_pct > 0]), collapse = ", ")` gain riders. `r str_c(str_to_title(upg$stn_name[upg$change_pct < 0]), collapse = ", ")` *lose* morning tap-ins despite the extra line, because several new stations open inside their former catchments and the added attraction does not offset the shorter walk to the new station. These counts are tap-ins only: transfers do not tap in, so platform and corridor loads at *every* upgraded interchange will still rise as passengers change between lines. For operators, the stations losing 15% or more of their boardings are where feeder-bus routes, and possibly train frequencies, should be reviewed first.

# Market areas before and after {#sec-market}

Following Chapter 18, each subzone is assigned to the station with the highest patronage probability (its **dominant station**), and the probability surface of one affected station is mapped before and after.

```{r}
#| label: market-areas
dominant <- function(shares) shares %>%
  group_by(SUBZONE_N) %>% slice_max(p_ij, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(SUBZONE_N, stn_code, p_ij)

dom_base <- dominant(shares_base)
dom_exp  <- dominant(shares_exp)

market_change <- origins_poly %>%
  left_join(dom_base %>% rename(dom_before = stn_code, p_before = p_ij), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  left_join(dom_exp %>% rename(dom_after = stn_code, p_after = p_ij), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  mutate(change = case_when(
    dom_before == dom_after ~ "Unchanged",
    dom_after %in% new_stations$stn_code ~ "Captured by a new station",
    TRUE ~ "Switched to another existing station"))

market_change %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(change) %>% summarise(subzones = n(), residents = fmt(sum(pop)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-market-switch

Essentially unpopulated subzones (fewer than 100 residents, or fewer than 100 per km², such as the Murai training area) are not shaded, so that large empty areas do not dominate the map. Click a subzone to see its old and new dominant station."
station_names <- bind_rows(st_drop_geometry(stations), st_drop_geometry(new_stations)) %>%

market_view <- market_change %>%
  populated_for_map() %>%

  mutate(before = str_to_title(station_names$stn_name[match(dom_before, station_names$stn_code)]),
         after = str_to_title(station_names$stn_name[match(dom_after, station_names$stn_code)])) %>%
  st_transform(4326)
pal_mkt <- colorFactor(c("#d95f02", "#7570b3"),
                       levels = c("Captured by a new station", "Switched to another existing station"))

base_leaflet() %>%
  addPolygons(data = market_view, group = "Subzones that change",
              fillColor = ~pal_mkt(change), fillOpacity = 0.6, color = "white", weight = 1,
              label = ~str_to_title(SUBZONE_N),
              popup = ~sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>Residents: %s<br>Before: %s (%s)<br>After: %s (%s)",
                               str_to_title(SUBZONE_N), comma(pop), before, pct(p_before, 0),
                               after, pct(p_after, 0))) %>%
  add_network(new_links = TRUE) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(data = st_transform(new_stations, 4326), group = "New stations",
                   radius = 3, color = "black", weight = 1, fillColor = "white", fillOpacity = 1,
                   label = ~str_to_title(stn_name)) %>%
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal_mkt, values = market_view$change, opacity = 0.8,
            title = "Dominant station") %>%
  layer_control(c("Subzones that change", "New stations", "Rail network"))
```

```{r}
  filter(change != "Unchanged") %>%
  mutate(before = str_to_title(station_names$stn_name[match(dom_before, station_names$stn_code)]),
```

```{r}
n_new <- sum(mc$change == "Captured by a new station")
```

Only `r n_new` of 286 populated subzones (`r fmt(pop_new)` residents) change their dominant station to a new one, and `r n_sw` more switch to a different existing station. The shifts form three groups:

- **West.** Teban Gardens and Penjuru Crescent (Jurong East) move to Pandan Reservoir, and Yuhua East to Toh Guan. Wenya, Boon Lay Place and Yunnan (Jurong West) move to Jurong West and Gek Poh. Bukit Batok West and Brickworks move to Bukit Batok West and Tengah Park, Peng Siang to Choa Chu Kang West, and Forest Hill to Tengah. The industrial subzones of Tukang, Liu Fang and Samulun move to their JRL stations.
- **North-east.** Serangoon North, Serangoon Garden and Seletar Hills move to Serangoon North and Tavistock. Trafalgar moves to the upgraded Hougang interchange, and Shangri-La and Upper Thomson to the upgraded Bright Hill interchange.
- **East.** Pasir Ris Drive, Flora Drive, Loyang East and West, Tampines North and Paya Lebar North move to Pasir Ris East, Loyang and Tampines North.

Everywhere else, including the whole of the city centre, the north and the south-west, the dominant station is unchanged. The new lines reshape market areas locally rather than system-wide.
